references.text: The psalmist washes his hands in innocence, reflecting the symbolic act of declaring oneself innocent of bloodguilt.
Reference to washing hands in innocence, symbolizing purity from guilt.
Pilate washed his hands before the crowd and declared himself innocent of Jesus' blood, an action that reflects the ritual in Deuteronomy.
Reuben warns his brothers not to shed blood, highlighting the seriousness of bloodguilt.
God demands accountability for human blood that has been shed, emphasizing the importance of having no part in bloodguilt.
The blood defiled the land, and atonement could only be made through the blood of the one who had shed it.
The purpose of the cities of refuge was to prevent innocent blood from being shed in the land.
David declares himself and his kingdom innocent of Abner's blood, similar to the declaration of innocence in Deuteronomy.
